Forecast audit · development history only

Check the forecast before trusting the allocation

Extreme raw forecasts can drive constrained portfolios. Compare their source, the full development history, and simple forecasts before interpreting an episode gain.

Start with all eligible months

Inspect each asset

See errors, forecast ranges, and the inputs behind the largest miss. All return forecasts use monthly decimals, displayed as percentages.

Use simple model references

The historical-mean forecast passes through the same BL pipeline. Prior-only allocation uses the same covariance, bounds, and trading rules.

Separate robustness from selection

Fixed input-clipping and no-policy checks quantify instability. They do not replace the original model or evaluate the reserved test.

Claims, credit and curve are condition variables. Growth/inflation × ANFCI/GPR interactions already belong to the original model.

Settings were recorded after the earlier research was seen and before this rerun. These are revised-history, exploratory results, not an independent confirmation.

What must be settled before the final test?

The investigation keeps the existing model rules and tuning grids. It does not choose a production winner. Before any reserved-period run, write down the selected inputs, preprocessing, tuning, allocation rules, forecast acceptance criteria and reporting metrics, then freeze their specification and code hashes. Confirm with the team whether 2023 onward remains unexamined; this code does not evaluate it.

Revised macro histories and assumed publication lags remain a separate limitation. A real-time vintage archive would require additional work, including ALFRED vintages where supported.

Monthly attribution versus the original model

Forecast, BL return and weight changes are selected minus original, in SPY / IEF / LQD order. Asset contributions use realized returns. Asset contributions plus the cost effect exactly equal the monthly net-return difference; they are not a compounded-period attribution.

Account for neighboring months

How uncertain is the monthly difference?

Paired block-bootstrap intervals compare each experiment with the original model, using the full common development history.

ExperimentMean monthly Δ95% interval · 3-month blocks6-month blocks12-month blocks

The same contiguous month blocks are sampled for both portfolios. These are unadjusted, exploratory percentile intervals for mean monthly net-return differences, conditional on the fitted strategies. They do not refit models, correct for trying multiple variants, or establish statistical significance. A short sample limits precision, especially with 12-month blocks.

Conditions can share information

Does credit overlap with ANFCI?

Credit featureCorrelation with ANFCI levelPast-only ANFCI projection R² vs. expanding mean

Projection uses known ANFCI level and monthly change, fitted on at least 24 earlier feature rows. A positive R² means it explains more credit variation than a historical-mean forecast; a negative R² means it explains less. This descriptive check uses revised histories and cannot establish that credit adds no return information. Compare the credit model's forecast errors and portfolio results as well.

Read the experiment

How these tests were built

Download research results (.json)
Longer training history

Adjusted SPY, IEF, and LQD prices begin in 2010. Training begins February 2015, requires 36 completed targets, and expands each month. BL waits for 12 earlier forecast errors.

One addition per experiment

The same Ridge → BL → allocation pipeline is rerun for the original and three added-condition versions. Fixed robustness checks change only preprocessing/shrinkage or the inclusion of policy fields. Claims, credit spread, and yield curve are tested separately, without choosing settings for each episode.

Trade after the decision

Decide at 8 p.m. New York on the last trading day. Enter the next trading day’s close and hold until the next rebalance close. The displayed holding month names the entry month.

Same portfolio rules

Starting mix 45 / 35 / 20. SPY 20–70%, IEF 15–60%, LQD 10–40%. Risk aversion 2.5, BL τ = 0.05. Costs are 5 bp per dollar traded from drifted holdings.

How this differs from the original MVP results

The research baseline is a fresh run, using longer price history, exact next-trading-close execution, completed targets only, and imputation fitted separately inside each tuning fold. Daily drawdowns also differ from the original monthly drawdowns. Compare signal experiments with the baseline on this page; the original MVP remains available in its tab.

Data limits and the reserved test

Claims, ANFCI, and GPR use revised histories with availability lags, not a complete real-time vintage archive. The workbook’s policy paths start in September 2019; earlier missing policy fields use training-only medians, or zero when the entire training column is missing. These are exploratory development results. No post-2022 strategy decisions are evaluated. The January 3, 2023 quote only closes December 2022’s holding interval.

These episode labels are evaluation windows, not information supplied to the model. The COVID market-shock window is not the same as the official recession chronology. Drawdown recovery is reported only within the selected window.

Units, forecast stability and audit settings

The combined robust-input sensitivity clips inputs to training-only 1st/99th percentiles and uses the fixed Ridge grid 1, 10, 100, 1000. Preprocessing and target-availability checks are repeated in every tuning fold. Separate clipping-only and shrinkage-only experiments isolate those two changes. The policy coverage safeguard disables each policy feature until it has 12 observed training values, inside every fold. This fixed sensitivity threshold does not certify a stable model. There is no cap on predicted returns. Without-policy sensitivity removes five policy-path fields over identical evaluation dates; it cannot reconstruct missing policy history.
